Convert ADRG Section Coverage to Evidence

Source: R/parsers_adrg.R
adrg_to_evidence.Rd

Scores an Analysis Data Reviewer's Guide for completeness against the standard section catalog and emits R4SUB evidence rows, one per section.

Usage

adrg_to_evidence(
  present,
  ctx,
  source_name = "adrg",
  source_version = NULL,
  standard = adrg_sections()
)

Arguments

present

A character vector of section_ids the guide contains, or a data.frame with a section_id column and a logical present column.

ctx

An r4sub_run_context.

source_name

Source label. Default "adrg"; use "sdrg" for a Study Data Reviewer's Guide.

source_version

Optional source version string.

standard

The section catalog to score against. Defaults to adrg_sections().

Value

An evidence data.frame, one row per standard section.

Details

ADRG and SDRG documents are Word or PDF, and reliable text extraction from them is out of scope for this package. adrg_to_evidence() therefore takes a structured summary of which sections a guide contains, which a document pipeline (or a human reviewer) can produce, and turns it into evidence. A present section passes. A missing required section fails at high severity; a missing recommended section warns at low severity. The rows land in the usability pillar, since the reviewer's guide is reviewer-facing documentation.

Examples

ctx <- suppressMessages(r4sub_run_context("STUDY1", "DEV"))
ev <- suppressMessages(adrg_to_evidence(c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"), ctx))
ev[, c("indicator_id", "severity", "result")]
#>    indicator_id severity result
#> 1      U-ADRG-1     high   pass
#> 2      U-ADRG-2     high   pass
#> 3      U-ADRG-3     high   pass
#> 4      U-ADRG-4     high   pass
#> 5      U-ADRG-5     high   pass
#> 6      U-ADRG-6     high   fail
#> 7    U-ADRG-1_3      low   warn
#> 8    U-ADRG-3_4      low   warn
#> 9    U-ADRG-4_2      low   warn
#> 10   U-ADRG-6_2      low   warn
